source_caption:
Backrooms was made for a reported $10 million and just opened to $118 million worldwide, including $81.4 million domestically. It is now the biggest opening weekend in A24 history, more than tripling the studio's previous record.

What's even more interesting is where it started. The Backrooms began with a single image posted anonymously online in 2019, showing an empty yellow room that slowly turned into one of the internet's most famous horror stories. Years later, online investigators traced the photo to a former store in Oshkosh, Wisconsin, photographed during renovations.

In 2022, teenager Kane Parsons turned that idea into a series of Backrooms short films on YouTube that exploded in popularity. Just a few years later, A24 handed him the keys to a feature film. Now 20 years old, Parsons has become one of the youngest directors ever to open a movie at number one at the US box office.

Seven years after an anonymous image appeared online, Backrooms has gone from internet legend to a record-breaking box office hit.

Did you know about Backrooms before the movie was announced?

source_details.synopsis: Backrooms is a 2026 American psychological horror film directed and co-scored by Kane Parsons in his feature directorial debut, and written by Will Soodik. It is based on Parsons's web series which was inspired by the "Backrooms" creepypasta. In the film, furniture store owner Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor) and his therapist Mary (Renate Reinsve) discover a dimension of seemingly endless liminal spaces accessed through the store's basement. Mark Duplass, Finn Bennett, and Lukita Maxwell also star. After uploading the web series in January 2022, Parsons was approached by several studios, including A24, about potentially adapting his series into a feature film.
